target_customer: Web designers, usability teams and advertisers paying per eye tracking study
problem: Eye tracking studies needed expensive hardware and labs; GazeHawk used ordinary webcams to run low-cost remote studies.
business_model: Pay per study using webcam testers

founders.name: Brian Krausz
founders.background_notes: Described in a 2010 research news item as a web usability specialist.

founders.name: Joe Gershenson
founders.background_notes: Described in a 2010 research news item as a web usability specialist.

exit.reason: Founders and team joined Facebook; product and technology were not part of the deal

technical_complexity.rationale: Webcam gaze estimation at consumer quality is a computer vision problem, harder than standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary tracking claimed but no patent or scale data found; a two person team.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it; Facebook hired the founders in April 2012 and the technology was to be sold separately.

market_need_then: Usability and ad evaluation studies relied on costly hardware eye trackers; GazeHawk pitched eye tracking for everyone with launch coverage in August 2010.

branding.domain_note: gazehawk.com; site later showed a founders-join-Facebook notice.

identity.voice_and_tone: positioned as eye tracking for everyone

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests watching eyes; sources show launch coverage but no brand-specific press or community.

outcome_analysis: GazeHawk offered webcam eye tracking studies from a two person team backed by YC and, per Patch, 500 Startups. In April 2012 the founders joined Facebook, a team acquisition, while the product and technology were left outside the deal and its fate is not documented.
notes: Competitor search returned only modern pages, so no dated 2010 competitors are listed. Seed round dated 2010-06 with no amount and investors 500 Startups, Y Combinator, Aaron Iba, Justin Yoshimura appears only on an aggregator; unverified and not recorded. Patch mentions 500 Startups backing and a six person team. Fueled says it launched in 2009, YC says 2010 batch. Founder education and prior employers not found.
